title: Capability registry for archive programs
description: A capability registry maps program names to their endpoints and declared abilities so archive tools can find each other. Registrations store name, version, endpoint, and a capability list; lookups match required capabilities against the registry and return candidates ranked by version. It is the phone book of the archive's programs. Use it so archive pipelines discover tools dynamically instead of hardcoding them.
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Health-checked service registry
description: A health-checked registry only advertises programs that recently proved they are alive, so discovery never returns dead tools. Registrants renew a heartbeat lease; a sweeper evicts entries whose lease expired, and lookups filter to healthy entries. The archive's tool ecosystem heals itself as programs come and go. Use it for long-running archive tool ecosystems with churn.
demo:
import time
reg = {"indexer": time.monotonic(), "old-parser": time.monotonic() - 999}
lease = 60
healthy = [n for n, t in reg.items() if time.monotonic() - t < lease]
print("healthy:", healthy)
assert healthy == ["indexer"]
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Hierarchical namespaces for program names
description: Hierarchical namespaces organize registry names into dotted paths so tools group by owner, team, or domain. Names like archive.index.v2 resolve through namespace nodes; lookups can target a subtree ('all archive.* tools') and policies attach at any level. Collisions vanish because full paths are unique. Use it to organize hundreds of archive tools without name clashes.
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Capability descriptor schema
description: A descriptor schema standardizes how archive programs declare what they do, their inputs, outputs, and limits. Descriptors are JSON documents validated against a schema: name, version, capabilities, input/output types, resource needs, and maturity level. Uniform descriptors let orchestrators reason about any tool. Use it so heterogeneous archive tools describe themselves consistently.
demo:
desc = {"name": "indexer", "version": "2.1", "caps": ["index"],
        "inputs": ["documents"], "outputs": ["postings"], "maturity": "stable"}
required = ["name", "version", "caps", "inputs", "outputs"]
missing = [k for k in required if k not in desc]
print("missing fields:", missing)
assert not missing
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Dependency manifests for archive tools
description: Dependency manifests declare every library and tool an archive program needs, making environments reproducible. The manifest lists pinned versions and compatible ranges; installers resolve the graph and lock exact versions. Two machines installing the same manifest get identical toolchains. Use it to make archive tool deployments reproducible.
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Interface contracts for tool APIs
description: Interface contracts specify a tool's API precisely — endpoints, parameters, and return shapes — so callers and tools evolve independently. Contracts are machine-readable (OpenAPI-style); validators check requests and responses against them in tests and at runtime. Breaking changes are caught before deployment. Use it to keep archive tool integrations stable.
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Gossip membership protocol
description: Gossip membership spreads program presence through randomized peer exchanges, discovering tools with no central server. Each node periodically picks a random peer and they reconcile membership lists; information spreads exponentially (like an epidemic) and failures are detected by missing heartbeats. It scales to thousands of nodes. Use it for decentralized archive tool discovery.
demo:
import random
random.seed(4)
nodes = {i: {i} for i in range(5)}
for _ in range(30):
    a, b = random.sample(range(5), 2)
    nodes[a] |= nodes[b]; nodes[b] |= nodes[a]
print("node 0 knows:", sorted(nodes[0]))
assert all(len(v) == 5 for v in nodes.values())
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: DNS-SD style local broadcast discovery
description: Broadcast discovery lets archive tools announce themselves on the local network so peers find them with zero configuration. Tools multicast announcements (name, capabilities, endpoint); listeners build a local registry from announcements and expire silent ones. It mirrors DNS Service Discovery semantics. Use it for plug-and-play tool discovery on local archive clusters.
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Heartbeat leases for registry entries
description: Heartbeat leases keep registry entries fresh: tools renew periodically and the registry drops the silent. Each registration carries an expiry timestamp refreshed by heartbeats; a background sweep removes expired entries. Lookups never see stale tools and crashed programs vanish automatically. Use it to keep any program registry accurate without manual cleanup.
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Semantic version resolution
description: Semver resolution picks the best tool version satisfying a constraint like ^2.1 or >=1.0,<3.0. Versions parse to (major, minor, patch) tuples; constraints compile to predicates, and the resolver picks the highest satisfying version. Caret and tilde ranges encode compatibility promises. Use it to select tool versions in archive pipelines safely.
demo:
def parse(v): return tuple(map(int, v.split(".")))
def caret_ok(v, base):
    return parse(v) >= parse(base) and parse(v)[0] == parse(base)[0]
avail = ["2.0.0", "2.3.1", "3.0.0"]
best = max([v for v in avail if caret_ok(v, "2.1.0")], key=parse)
print("resolved:", best)
assert best == "2.3.1"

title: Deprecation policy enforcement
description: Deprecation policy phases out old tool versions on a schedule instead of breaking callers overnight. Versions move through active, deprecated (warns but works), and retired (removed); the registry announces transitions ahead of time and pipelines pin or migrate. Orderly sunsets replace surprise breakage. Use it to evolve the archive's tool ecosystem without outages.
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Compatibility matrix for tool versions
description: A compatibility matrix records which tool versions work together so the registry can veto bad combinations. The matrix maps (tool-a-version, tool-b-version) pairs to supported/unsupported; installers check the matrix before deploying a set. It prevents integration failures from version drift. Use it when archive pipelines combine many independently-versioned tools.
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Registration audit log
description: An audit log records every registry change — who registered what, when — for accountability and forensics. Append-only entries with timestamps, actor, and action; the log is hash-chained so tampering is detectable. Investigations trace any tool's lifecycle. Use it to make the program registry trustworthy and debuggable.
demo:
import hashlib
log, prev = [], "GENESIS"
def record(actor, action):
    global prev
    h = hashlib.md5((prev + actor + action).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    log.append({"actor": actor, "action": action, "chain": h}); prev = h
record("ops", "register indexer"); record("ops", "retire parser-1")
print("entries:", len(log), "| chained:", log[1]["chain"] != log[0]["chain"])
assert len(log) == 2

title: Access-scoped registry views
description: Scoped views show each archive tenant only the registry entries they may use, enforcing least privilege. Entries carry visibility scopes; lookups filter by the caller's scopes before returning results. Internal tools stay invisible to external tenants. Use it for multi-tenant archive tool ecosystems.
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Registry search index
description: A search index over registry metadata lets users find tools by capability words, not just exact names. The registry tokenizes names, descriptions, and capabilities into an inverted index; queries rank matches by field weights. Discovery becomes exploratory instead of exact. Use it to make large program registries browsable.
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice
